messages:
Oncall-Bot: Pager: P1 continuous-batching latency spike on prod region-us-east1 — error-rate and tail latency increased. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. alloc_group: runtime-prod, metric: tail_p99_resp_time > 2000ms
Alex C.: I’m on it. seeing a big queueing backlog on the serving nodes, +KV cache size exploded on a subset of pods. linking graphs: https://grafana.redwood/v/serve/continuous-batch?panel=queue_length
Sylvia: Confirmed — KV cache memory per-gpu jumped ~6x on nodes hosting active rtx pool, evictions thrashing. CPU in the model workers is pegged, and microbatch processing time doubled (context: model kv cache hot-path).
Jamie: Any recent rollout that touched batching? I remember we pushed a config change yesterday to raise max_batch_delay to 12ms for latency-sensitive routes.
Priya: Yeah that rollout included an opt-in for continuous-batching defaults. Might be interacting with certain request size distributions and causing big prefix-KV retention.
Tariq: Early mitigation idea: force per-route override to disable continuous batching for the affected model or set max_batch_size=1 for hot routes. That should collapse batching and stop queue amplification.
Alex C.: Agreed. Also consider lowering max_batch_delay to 2ms temporarily. Which route is hottest? route_id: /v1/generate/redwood-xxl (mostly NA customers).
Sylvia: Customers impacted: 3 enterprise tenants showing 3-10x p99 latency; traffic volume concentrated to 4 pods. I’m seeing kv_cache_size growth tied to long-lived prefixes — seems like repeated long contexts not evicting properly.
Ops-Bot: Deploy bot: rolling-config-change initiated by alex-c at 2003141630: set route /v1/generate/redwood-xxl batching.continuous=false. See change-id: cfg-2003141630.
Jamie: Nice — also prepare a quick revert plan if that makes latency worse. We should not degrade throughput for other tenants.
Priya: Command to patch route config (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/routes/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate/redwood-xxl","batching":{"continuous":false,"max_batch_delay_ms":2}}'
```
Tariq: I’ll tail logs on the affected pods and watch for backlog drain. kubectl exec -it model-worker-7 -- tail -n 200 /var/log/worker/requests.log
Alex C.: Rolling out now. Starting with 2 pods behind the load balancer.
Sylvia: After change, KV cache growth stopped on pod-7 and pod-8 within 40s. queue_length dropped from 120->18 on those pods. p99 CPU fell ~30%.
Jamie: Are we seeing error rate improvements upstream? any 5xx spikes?
Ops-Bot: Metric: p99_resp_time route /v1/generate/redwood-xxl: 2400ms -> 680ms in 2 minutes post-change. 5xxs dropped to baseline.
Priya: Good. But we should be cautious: disabling continuous batching increases per-token cost. We need a follow-up ticket to tune kernel/quantization pairing and also look at bug in KV eviction.
Tariq: Observed behavior: when continuous batching hit a particular concurrency pattern, microbatches tried to hold KV entries longer expecting future merges, causing high memory retention and eviction churn. Repro steps in staging: replay ramped-concurrency with long prefixes.
Alex C.: Action items captured:
- hotfix applied (continuous batching disabled on route) — mitigated.
- run controlled repro in staging with long prefixes + high concurrency to hit the kv retention bug (owner: Tariq)
- evaluate safer defaults: lower max_batch_delay and smaller max_batch_size (owner: Jamie)
- RCA: investigate eviction policy for prefix-KV and whether LRU is being starved by long-running prefixes (owner: Sylvia)
- Customer comms: CS to notify impacted tenants (owner: Priya)
Sylvia: Noted a small regression: overall throughput for that route dropped ~18%, but latency stable. We might need to scale dedicated pool or route to a higher concurrency tier temporarily.
Jamie: Can we enable per-customer routing to spread load across more pods? That’s a quick capacity mitigation: add routing weight for spare nodes.
Ops-Bot: Routing change queued: route-weight-increase for route /v1/generate/redwood-xxl to add 2 extra pods. Change-id: route-weight-2003141745.
Priya: CS update drafted: "We observed tail latency and queuing on a production route, mitigated by disabling continuous batching for affected model. Customers may see slightly lower throughput but normal latency. Full RCA to follow."
Alex C.: Posting incident in incidents channel and assigning severity P1 -> P2 transition document. I’ll hand off to oncall-night at 2003142100. If anything regresses, page me.
Tariq: Leaving notes in the incident doc: repro script, logs, and a small snapshot of kv cache metrics.
Jamie: Plan to run an A/B test with reduced max_batch_delay=3ms combined with adaptive eviction in staging next week.
Priya: Marking impacted customers list and scheduling postmortem with CS + infra + runtime next biz day.
Oncall-Bot: Incident created: INC-200314-003. Severity P2. Handoff: alex-c -> oncall-night at 2003142100.
Alex C.: Thanks team — summary: live mitigation via route override worked, primary driver appears to be continuous-batching interaction with long-lived prefixes causing KV cache blowup and queueing gridlock at high concurrency. RCA items assigned. Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:
